module_title: Doctrines of Election, Ostensible Ownership & Lis Pendens
introduction: This intermediate tier explores the powerful equitable doctrines embedded in the TPA. It dissects how the law handles unauthorized transfers, protects bona fide purchasers, and freezes property rights during pending litigation.

core_concepts.title: Doctrine of Election (Section 35)
core_concepts.description:
Based on the maxim: 'You cannot approbate and reprobate' (You cannot accept the benefit and reject the burden).
- The Rule: If a person professes to transfer property which he has no right to transfer, and as part of the SAME transaction confers a benefit on the true owner of that property, the real owner must 'elect' (choose).
- The Choice: The owner can either accept the transaction (give up his property and take the benefit) OR reject the transaction (keep his property but forfeit the benefit).
- Example: A sells B's house to C for 10 Lakhs. In the same deed, A gives B a car worth 15 Lakhs. B must elect to either take the car and let C have the house, or keep the house and refuse the car.

core_concepts.title: Ostensible Owner (Section 41)
core_concepts.description:
An 'Ostensible Owner' is a person who has all the indicia (appearance) of ownership but is not the real owner (e.g., a Benamidar).
- The Rule: If an ostensible owner transfers property with the express or implied consent of the real owner, the transfer is VALID, provided the transferee (buyer) acted in **good faith** and took **reasonable care** to verify the title.
- Protection: This protects innocent third-party buyers who pay value for property from a person the real owner allowed to act like the boss.

core_concepts.title: Doctrine of Lis Pendens (Section 52)
core_concepts.description:
Based on the maxim: *Pendente lite nihil innovetur* (During litigation, nothing new should be introduced).
- The Rule: When a suit or proceeding regarding the right to any immovable property is pending in a competent court, the property CANNOT be transferred or dealt with by any party to the suit to affect the rights of the other party.
- Consequence: If A and B are fighting over a house in court, and A sells it to C, C's purchase is completely subject to the final court decree. If B wins the case, C loses the house. (It doesn't make the transfer void, but makes it subservient to the court's decision).

core_concepts.title: Condition Restraining Alienation (Section 10)
core_concepts.description:
The law encourages the free flow of property.
- The Rule: If property is transferred subject to a condition that ABSOLUTELY restrains the transferee from parting with or disposing of their interest, that **condition is void**, but the transfer itself remains valid. (e.g., A sells a house to B on the condition B can never sell it to anyone. B gets the house, and the condition is deleted by law).

important_entities.name: Bona Fide Purchaser for Value
important_entities.key_fact: The ultimate protected entity in Equity.
important_entities.significance: Under Section 41 (Ostensible Owner), the law will only protect the buyer if they prove they acted 'Bona Fide' (in good faith), paid 'Value' (consideration), and made a reasonable inquiry into the title. A buyer who acts negligently gets no protection.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: For the Doctrine of Election (Sec 35) to apply, the transfer of the property and the conferring of the benefit MUST be part of the **SAME transaction/document**. If A transfers B's property to C in January, and gives B a car in February via a separate document, B does NOT have to elect. B can keep the car and the house.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Pending Suit, Competent Court, Specific Property
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: For Section 52 to freeze the transfer, the suit must not be collusive, it must be in a competent court, and the right to *that specific immovable property* must be directly in question.

exam_strategy_tips: If a Judiciary question asks 'Which maxim forms the basis of Section 52 of the TPA?', the answer is **Pendente lite nihil innovetur**.
